title: ICS Attack Path Explorer
description: Interactive p5.js MicroSim of a Purdue-model industrial network. Toggle segmentation controls (DMZ broker, allowlisting, MFA jump host, read-only historian, disable RDP) and run an attack from Level 5 to the Level 1 PLCs to see how path length, time to compromise, and blast radius change.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

educational.topic: Industrial control system segmentation and the Purdue model
learningObjectives: Apply segmentation controls to a Purdue-model network with an attacker at Level 5.
Analyze how each control changes attack path length, time to compromise, and blast radius.
Reason about which IT/OT chokepoints contain an attacker and why layering matters against a skilled adversary.
educational.prerequisites: Basic networking and the idea of lateral movement; familiarity with the Purdue model is helpful but not required.

pedagogical.assessment: Students find the minimal set of controls that fully contains the attacker at Attacker Skill 5 and again at Skill 10, then explain why the answer differs.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing a single segmentation control is sufficient to protect OT.
Assuming a read-only control that does not fully block the attacker provides no value.
